raw_response:
Looking at my situation: I've got about 12 mu of flat land here in Quzhou. My family has grown winter wheat and summer maize on this land for three generations. It's what I know, it's what the land here is suited for, and the local grain traders and cooperative always buy it. I'm not going to try something new and risk a bad year.

After the maize comes off in late September, I prep the ground with the rotary tiller and get wheat in by mid-October. I'll buy certified seed from the county seed station — Jimai or Kenong variety, whichever the station recommends this year. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea in spring when the wheat is jointing. I'll pump groundwater three times: the winter irrigation before freeze, again at jointing, and one more at grain filling if it looks dry. I'll spray herbicide in December and then fungicide plus insecticide in April when I see rust or aphids starting.

Once wheat is off in June I plant maize right away — I can't afford to lose time. I use hybrid seed, Xianyu 335 or Zhengdan 958. I plant directly into the stubble without tilling again — saves diesel and the soil is still loose. Summer rains usually carry the crop but I'll irrigate twice just in case. Herbicide goes on right after planting, and I'll spray once more for corn borer if I see egg masses on the leaves.

That's my year. Two crops, same 10 mu, proven system. I keep 2 mu near the house for our family vegetable garden but that's not a commercial crop.
